verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The right-hand bound is stated verbatim by weight_parameter_radial_shift_ratio, with ε in place of ρ. As in (B.9) the exact middle member is split: coreWeight_parameter_shift is the equality coreWeight i (k+1) = (20/ε)(i+1) coreWeight (i+1) k, i.e. the paper's leading factor (20/ρ)(i+1) exactly, and the two square-decay quotients squareDecay i / squareDecay (i+1) = (i+2)^2/(i+1)^2 and squareDecay (k+1) / squareDecay k = (k+1)^2/(k+2)^2 are the paper's remaining two factors, stated in the repository only in inequality form (≤ 4 and ≤ 1 respectively); recovering the displayed equality is one unfolding of squareDecay. The product 20 · 4 · 1 = 80 gives the paper's (80/ρ)(i+1). I checked the binomial bookkeeping behind the (i+1): binom(i+k+1,k+1)/binom(i+k+1,k) = (i+1)/(k+1) cancels the (k+1) from the factorial, which is what coreWeight_parameter_shift asserts. Lean quantifies over all i, k : ℕ and all real ε > 0.
